title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 49
paragraphs: After this, with great sacrifices he sought to win the favor of the god at Delphi: for of every kind of animal fit for sacrifice he offered three thousand, and he heaped up couches overlaid with gold and with silver, and cups of gold, and robes of purple, and tunics, making of them a great pyre, and he burnt all this up, hoping by these means to win the god all the more to the side of the Lydians. He also proclaimed to all the Lydians that every one of them should make sacrifice with whatever he had. And when he had finished the sacrifice, he melted down a vast quantity of gold, and from it he wrought half-plinths, making them six palms in length, three in breadth, and one in height. Their number was one hundred and seventeen. Of these, four were of pure gold, weighing two and a half talents each; the others were of gold alloyed with silver, weighing two talents each. He also had made an image of a lion of pure gold, weighing ten talents. This lion, when the temple at Delphi was being burned down, fell from off the half-plinths, for it had been set upon them, and is now placed in the treasury of the Corinthians, weighing six and a half talents, since three and a half talents had been melted away from it.
